title: Policy
description: An ordered set of rules evaluated at three points in the execution path (ADR-008). Earlier drafts of this file described approval thresholds, scope allow/deny lists and retention buckets as three unrelated sections; those are all expressible as rules, and having one rule form means one evaluation path, one decision record, and one coverage measurement rather than three.

defaultEffect.description: Applied when no rule matches. `allow` today — but the evaluation is still recorded as unmatched, which is the number ADR-014 wants reported. Flipping this to `deny` closes the world and should only happen once coverage justifies it.

PolicyPoint.description: Enforcement belongs at the seams, not in one chokepoint — each seam knows something the others do not.

PolicyCondition.description: Every condition is optional. A rule with none matches everything — legal, and exactly what the vacuous-rule report exists to surface.

capabilities.description: Capability id, or a prefix glob ending in `*`. Deliberately not full regex: a policy language that can express anything is one nobody can audit.

tags.description: Tags carried by the inputs. This is how `untrusted` content reaches policy.

nonIdempotent.description: Fires when the tool is not declared idempotent. Absent information counts as non-idempotent: ADR-016 requires an explicit declaration, and the safe reading of silence is the one that cannot replay a side effect.

priority.description: Lower numbers win. Ties break by severity — deny over require_approval over allow — so a misordered policy fails closed.

rules.description: Content fetched from the open web must not drive a browser or a device.
